newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia warns on Cambodia fighting.
newsitem.headline: Australia warns on Cambodia fighting.

text.p: Australia on Thursday voiced concern about escalating violence in Cambodia, warning it could threaten aid to the impoverished southeast Asian country.

Foreign Minister Alexander Downer, due to visit Phnom Penh soon, told parliament he would press Cambodia's leaders to renew efforts to ease political tensions that erupted into bloody fighting on the streets of the capital, Phnom Penh, this week.

"I'll impress upon them that the maintenance of the rule of law is critical to the implementation of the (1991) Paris Peace Accords and continuing support of donors in Cambodia's reconstruction process," Downer said.
"I'll also underline the importance of the Cambodian parties renewing efforts to resolve political tensions."
No date has yet been set for the visit.
Downer said he was concerned at the increasing violence as the decades-old threat from Khmer Rouge guerrillas was waning.

"Inflammatory statements by Cambodian leaders and their race to secure military and factional support, including from defecting Khmer Rouge forces, have, unfortunately, only added to these tensions," he said.
Cambodia's co-premiers -- Prince Norodom Ranariddh and former communist Hun Sen -- have for months been locked in a bitter feud over power-sharing in their coalition government.
Tensions spilled over into a 90-minute gunfight in Phnom Penh on Tuesday between forces loyal to Ranariddh and Hun Sen.
The worsening violence comes amid unconfirmed reports that reviled Khmer Rouge strongman Pol Pot has surrendered to former comrades-in-arms.
Downer welcomed the possible capture of Pol Pot, under whose brutal 1970s rule at least one million Cambodians died through executions, torture, disease, starvation and overwork.

"The demise of the Khmer Rouge armed threat to Cambodian politics would be a welcome end to a bloody chapter in Cambodia's history," he said, urging an international war crimes trial for Pol Pot and other Khmer Rouge leaders.

Australia was a major force in securing the Paris peace deal that ended decades of war between Hun Sen's then government and guerrilla factions including the Khmer Rouge and royalist forces before U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.
